attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: An observation about an ongoing trend ('quickly becoming'). The IP clause is hedged ('not clear'), and the contract correctly does not score it on its own.

contract.note: 'Commodities' is undefined. The reading (many comparable, substitutable suppliers, launch through 2023) is ordinary, though it leans toward 'are commodities' rather than 'becoming'. The result depends on whether proliferation or the frontier performance gap is weighted more.

evidence.note: AI Index: 149 foundation models in 2023, more than double 2022, and most of them open. Consistent with fast proliferation of substitutes.
Closed models kept a median 24.2% benchmark lead over open models in 2023, so frontier models were not interchangeable. This does not compare OpenAI with Google.
Weeks after the post, Meta released LLaMA, which beat GPT-3 on most benchmarks. Others replicated earlier OpenAI capability quickly.
OpenAI earned about $80M/month in 2023. This hints at pricing power but measures commoditization only indirectly.

reviews.rationale: The trend toward many substitutable LLMs holds: model releases doubled, most were open, and LLaMA quickly matched GPT-3. But closed frontier models kept a clear measured lead through 2023, so leading models were not yet easily replaced. The proliferation part holds; the substitutability-at-the-frontier part does not.
